subject: Longitudinal invariance - latent variable correlating greater than 1 across time

messages.author: ccaed8d972a5ce78
messages.subject: Longitudinal invariance - latent variable correlating greater than 1 across time
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm testing for longitudinal measurement invariance across three time points but the models at each stage of the invariance test (i.e. baseline, loading invariance, and threshold invariance) are all being flagged with the warning: "covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite". When I inspect the covariance matrix and the corresponding correlation matrix, I find that the correlations for factor 1 across the three time points are all greater than 1 (e.g., correlating factor 1 at time 1 with factor 1 at time 2).   

So that appears to be the problem causing the warning. My question is what I should do about that? Do I need to change the model specification in some way or can I ignore the warning and interpret the change in model fit across the three models?

The cfa model I'm testing is a 2-factor solution from a measure with 14 items (four items load on factor 1 and the other ten load on factor 2) over three time periods with a sample size of 722 (the sample size is lower at the second and third time points). My syntax is adapted from the supplemental materials from this article: https://doi.org/10.1037/met0000075 

Any help would be much appreciated.

Regards
Simon

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: Re: Longitudinal invariance - latent variable correlating greater than 1 across time
parts:
Hello Simon,

An interesting question that puzzles me too. However, are you sure that the correlations are not regression coefficients from correlating factors? It looks like your analysis was based on covariance matrix. Those could be greater than 1 I presume? Are you looking at the standardized loadings? If not, that could explain values >1?

Thx. for the article link. Something I need to get into.

Regards,
Guido

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Longitudinal invariance - latent variable correlating greater than 1 across time
parts:
It is possible that simple structure does not hold for your model.  Sometimes I see Heywood cases disappear after imposing more restrictive invariance constraints.  If that doesn't make the problem go away, then you should carefully consider your item content for any possible minor/method factors (e.g., similar item wording) that could account for why there is more shared variance across occasions than your model currently allows for (which is why your factor correlations are struggling to be higher).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
